function_v0.doc:
Cancels the scheduled operation identified by `(caller, target, function,
args)`. `canceller` must be the operation's scheduler (`caller`), an
effective `ADMIN_ROLE` member, or an effective member of the guardian
role of the function's required role. Returns the canceled nonce.

# Errors

* [`AccessManagerError::OperationNotScheduled`] - No pending operation
exists for the given parameters.
* [`AccessManagerError::UnauthorizedCancel`] - `canceller` is not allowed
to cancel the operation.
function_v0.name: cancel

function_v0.doc:
Relays a call to `function` on `target` with `args`, on behalf of
`caller`, returning the target's return value.

`caller` must currently be allowed to call the function (see
[`AccessManager::can_call`]). Because the manager is the owner/admin of
`target`, the target authorizes the relayed call. If the caller holds the
required role behind a non-zero execution delay, the call must have been
scheduled via [`AccessManager::schedule`] and its delay must have elapsed;
the matching scheduled operation is consumed.

# Errors

* [`AccessManagerError::TargetClosed`] - The target is closed.
* [`AccessManagerError::Unauthorized`] - The caller lacks the role.
* [`AccessManagerError::OperationNotScheduled`] - The caller has an
execution delay but no matching scheduled operation.
* [`AccessManagerError::OperationNotReady`] - The scheduled operation's
delay has not yet elapsed.
* [`AccessManagerError::OperationExpired`] - The scheduled operation has
expired and must be scheduled again.
function_v0.name: execute

function_v0.doc: Returns whether `caller` may call `function` on `target` right now, and\nthe execution delay that applies.
function_v0.name: can_call

function_v0.doc: Returns whether `account` is an effective member of `role` and the\nexecution delay attached to that membership.
function_v0.name: has_role

function_v0.doc:
Schedules a delayed call to `function` on `target` with `args`, on behalf
of `caller`, so it can later be run through [`AccessManager::execute`]
once the caller's execution delay has elapsed.

`when` is the desired execution timestamp; pass `0` to schedule at the
earliest permitted time (`now + execution_delay`). Returns the operation
id and its nonce.

# Errors

* [`AccessManagerError::TargetClosed`] - The target is closed.
* [`AccessManagerError::Unauthorized`] - The caller is not a member of
the required role, or holds it with no execution delay (in which case
it can call [`AccessManager::execute`] directly without scheduling).
* [`AccessManagerError::InvalidScheduleTime`] - `when` is earlier than
`now + execution_delay`.
* [`AccessManagerError::OperationAlreadyScheduled`] - An identical
operation is already scheduled and still pending.
function_v0.name: schedule

function_v0.doc:
Grants `role` to `account` with the given `execution_delay`.

`caller` must be an effective member of `role`'s admin role. The grant
becomes effective after the role's grant delay; for an account that is
already a member, only the execution delay is updated.

`PUBLIC_ROLE` cannot be granted (everyone holds it implicitly).
